safety_verdicts.content: Patient has a history of Type 2 diabetes.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated documents diabetes mellitus but does not specify Type 2 (pmh-001, assessment-002).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not specifying Type 2 diabetes reduces clinical clarity for risk stratification and appropriate chronic disease management (e.g., typical therapies, complication screening), though it is unlikely to change immediate dermatitis care. It can also lead to downstream documentation/coding inaccuracies and missed diabetes-specific considerations.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold lists metformin, but Generated does not mention metformin or any diabetes medication.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting metformin from the medication list compromises medication reconciliation and can contribute to inappropriate prescribing decisions (e.g., interactions, duplicate therapy) or missed opportunities to assess diabetes control and adherence. Harm is usually limited to additional follow-up/clarification unless it leads to a concrete prescribing error.

safety_verdicts.content: Painful, cracked, dry skin on hands/fingers
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold explicitly states 'No pain' (hpi-002), while this generated chief complaint states the hand skin is painful.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting pain when the gold standard indicates no pain can misrepresent severity and may prompt unnecessary escalation (e.g., concern for infection or more aggressive therapy). In most cases this results in inaccurate clinical picture and potential extra evaluation rather than major injury.
